title: BPP pledge_amend request (DESIGN.md §9.5, §14.8; registry R5 participant)
description: Mutation (meta required). An amendment is a new PledgeProposal naming the prior Pledge, revision, and terms digest (amendment_of, verbatim §9.3); one compare-and-swap successor slot prevents divergent current successors — a conflict fails stale_revision. It needs all currently required seats again, so the full terms are restated; proposed_pledgor_ref/beneficiary_ref carry over from the prior revision when absent (registry rule) — gap note G23. Acceptance atomically supersedes the old revision, fences incompatible episodes and unstarted effects, reallocates budgets, and creates a new PledgeWorkstream generation where required (§9.5). Stage-capable (R5).

amendment_of.description: Names the prior Pledge, revision, and terms digest (§9.3 amendment_of, verbatim).

budget_request_set.description: Opaque body pending the BPA-1 policy-algebra slice (ADR-0001); gap note G10.

allowed_manifestation_selector.description: Opaque body pending the BPA-1 policy-algebra slice (ADR-0001); gap note G10.

delegation_ceiling.description: Opaque body pending the BPA-1 policy-algebra slice (ADR-0001); gap note G10.

cancellation_terms.description: Opaque body pending the BPA-1 policy-algebra slice (ADR-0001); gap note G10.

identifier.description: Opaque visible-ASCII identifier, at most 128 bytes (§14.9).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§14.2 rejects unsafe integers).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant with Z offset. DESIGN.md does not fix a timestamp wire encoding; this derivation freezes with the bundle (gap note G3).

class.description: Digest class per the §14.2 table; substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.

key_id.description: Key id for keyed classes (raw HMAC keys and per-object salts are never part of a DigestRef).

digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef (§14.2): every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash.

mutationMeta.description: MutationMeta (§14.2). Required on every mutation; update operations additionally supply expected_revision (registry rule enforced in code, not expressible here).
